beats.spoken: Parabens are banned in the EU. You hear that a lot. But it's only partly true.

Parabens are a family of preservatives. They help stop bacteria and mould from growing in cosmetics. That's how the US Food and Drug Administration describes them. The most common, according to the FDA, are methyl, propyl, butyl and ethylparaben.

In the EU, Regulation 358 from 2014 removed five parabens: isopropyl, isobutyl, phenyl, benzyl and pentyl paraben. There wasn't enough data to assess their safety. The committee said their risk to people couldn't be assessed.
Methylparaben and ethylparaben are different. The EU's scientific committee confirmed they are safe at the permitted maximum concentration, so they stay allowed.
From October 2014, new products with the five substances could no longer be placed on the market. From July 2015, they could no longer be sold at all.

nodes.text: 30 October: no new products placed on the market

beats.spoken: Here's how to read the list: methylparaben or ethylparaben is allowed. The five removed names should not show up on new stock in the EU. And labels often list more than one paraben.
Read the names first, then judge. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
